problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=5x(t)-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above and its trajectory passing through the point $(1,-1)$ in the phase space of the system. What is the tangent vector to the trajectory at this point?

feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+4y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2x(t)+2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above and its trajectory passing through the point $(3,-1)$ in the phase space of the system. What is the tangent vector to the trajectory at this point?
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the $xy$-coordinate plane is called the *phase plane* of the system. A particular solution of an initial value problem is called a *trajectory* (or *orbit*).

In our case, the trajectory (solution) passes through the point $(x,y)=(3,-1)$ in the phase space. Substituting the coordinates of this point into the equations of our system, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} & =-x+4y \\  & =-3+4(-1) \\  & =-3-4 \\  & =-7 \\ {y}^{′} & =2x+2y \\  & =2(3)+2(-1) \\  & =6-2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent vector to the trajectory is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} \\ {y}^{′}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
